name: REF102CU
title: 10 V precision voltage reference
summary: The REF102 is a 10 V series reference built on a buried zener and a laser-trimmed amplifier, with no heater. Three grades set initial error (to ±2.5 mV) and drift (to 2.5 ppm/°C); it runs from 11.4 V to 36 V on 1.4 mA maximum, sources 10 mA and sinks 5 mA. A Trim pin allows ±3 % adjustment and a Noise Reduction pin takes a filter capacitor.

circuits.title: Basic connection with star wiring
circuits.description: The supply sits across V+ and Com with a 1 µF tantalum capacitor beside it; each load returns by its own lead to the Com pin, a star at pin 4. Lead resistance up to a few ohms in the supply and common leads has negligible effect; 0.1 Ω in an output or load-return lead gives 1 mV of error (0.01 % of 10 V) at the full 10 mA load.
notes: Lead resistance up to a few ohms between the supply and pin 2, and between pin 4 and ground, has negligible effect.
A 0.1 Ω series resistance in a lead from pin 6 to a load or from a load back to pin 4 produces 1 mV of error at 10 mA, 0.01 % of 10 V.

circuits.title: Output voltage adjust
circuits.description: A 20 kΩ potentiometer across the output and common drives the Trim pin from its wiper, giving at least ±300 mV of adjustment with little added drift. A 1 µF tantalum capacitor bypasses V+.

parts.note: potentiometer; pins 1 and 2 the ends, W the wiper

notes: Minimum range ±300 mV.

circuits.title: Output voltage fine adjust
circuits.description: As the plain adjust circuit, with a 1 MΩ resistor RS between the potentiometer wiper and the Trim pin. The range shrinks to about ±25 mV and the resolution rises.

parts.note: potentiometer; pins 1 and 2 the ends, W the wiper

notes: Range typically ±25 mV.

circuits.title: −10 V reference, resistor biased
circuits.description: The output pin is grounded and the common pin is the −10 V output, returned to −15 V through RS. V+ is 1.4 V to 26 V. RS satisfies 1.4mA < (5V − IL)/RS < 5.4mA, IL the load current at the −10 V output.

circuits.title: Precision −10 V reference with OPA227
circuits.description: The REF102 output pin feeds the OPA227 inverting input through a 2 kΩ resistor, with 1000 pF from that input to the amplifier output; the non-inverting input is grounded. The amplifier output drives the common pin, which is the −10 V output. V+ is 1.4 V to 26 V.

circuits.title: +10 V reference buffered to ±20 mA
circuits.description: An OPA227 voltage follower on the output pin lets the load draw or return up to 20 mA; the follower also makes the output more immune to transients.
notes: −20mA < IL < +20mA

circuits.title: +10 V reference boosted to 100 mA with a PNP
circuits.description: A 220 Ω resistor sits between V+ and the REF102 supply pin; a 2N2905 PNP has its emitter on V+, its base on the supply pin and its collector on the output. The load current runs from −5 mA to +100 mA.
notes: −5mA < IL < +100mA

circuits.title: +10 V reference with a resistor carrying the typical load
circuits.description: A resistor R1 from V+ to the output supplies the expected load current, so the REF102 only handles the variation: the load may run from 5 mA below to 10 mA above its typical value.
notes: IL(MAX) = IL(TYP) + 10mA; IL(MIN) = IL(TYP) − 5mA.

circuits.title: Strain gauge conditioner for a 350 Ω bridge
circuits.description: The REF102 runs from +15 V; its output is the +5 V node and its common pin, driven by the OPA227 output, is the −5 V node across a 350 Ω bridge. One bridge midpoint goes to the OPA227 inverting input, whose non-inverting input is grounded. A 357 Ω, 1/2 W resistor joins +15 V to the +5 V node and another joins the −5 V node to −15 V. An INA126 with gain resistor RG takes the two bridge midpoints and gives VOUT ×100.
notes: 28 mA flows in the upper 357 Ω resistor and 28.5 mA into the bridge at the +5 V node.
OPA227 pins: 2 inverting input, 3 non-inverting input, 6 output. INA126 pins: 5 inverting input, 10 non-inverting input, 8 output.

circuits.title: ±10 V reference with INA105
circuits.description: The INA105 with its four 25 kΩ resistors works as a unity-gain inverter: its pin 2 takes the +10 V output, pins 1 and 3 sit at ground, and pins 5 and 6 tied together give −10 V.
notes: INA105 internal resistors 25 kΩ each.

circuits.title: Positive precision current source
circuits.description: R runs from the REF102 output pin to the top of the load, which also feeds the OPA277 non-inverting input; the OPA277 output and inverting input drive the REF102 common pin. IOUT = 10 V / R with R ≥ 1 kΩ; the load's other end goes to ground or to −VS.
notes: IOUT = 10V / R, R ≥ 1 kΩ.

circuits.title: Stacked references for +10 V, +20 V and +30 V
circuits.description: Three REF102s in series: each upper unit's common sits on the output of the one below, and each one's V+ takes the output of the one above it, the top one running from 31.4 V to 56 V. The outputs are +10 V, +20 V and +30 V.
notes: Outputs come in multiples of 10 V.
Supply between 10n + 1.4 V and 10n + 26 V, n the number of REF102s.
Each REF102 stays within its +10 mA, −5 mA output rating, counting the current it delivers to the unit below.

circuits.title: ±5 V reference with INA105
circuits.description: The output pin gives +5 V and the common pin −5 V. INA105 pin 2 takes the +5 V output, pins 1 and 3 go to ground, and pins 5 and 6 join the common pin.

circuits.title: +5 V and +10 V reference with INA105
circuits.description: The +10 V output feeds INA105 pin 3; pin 1 goes to ground and pins 2, 5 and 6 tie together, so the INA105 halves the reference and gives +5 V beside the +10 V output.

circuits.title: Very low noise reference averaging N units
circuits.description: N REF102 outputs are averaged through a 2 kΩ resistor each into the non-inverting input of an OPA227. R2 (2 kΩ) feeds back from the output node to the inverting input with C2 (1 µF) from the inverting input to the amplifier output; R1 (1 kΩ) and C1 (1 µF) filter the amplifier output into VREF. The average of the N outputs appears at VREF and its noise falls by √N. Three units are shown: (1), (2) and (N).
notes: VREF = (VOUT1 + VOUT2 … VOUTN) / N.
eN = 5 µVPP / √N, f = 0.1 Hz to 1 MHz.
OPA227 pins: 2 inverting input, 3 non-inverting input.

circuits.title: Noise test circuit
circuits.description: The reference under test is AC-coupled through 100 µF into an OPA227 non-inverting stage with 15.8 kΩ to ground at its input; 2 kΩ feedback over 20 Ω to ground sets a gain of 100. An 8 kΩ, 2 µF low-pass follows before the oscilloscope. The band runs from 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz.
notes: Gain = 100V/V; f−3dB = 0.1Hz and 10Hz.

operation.text: A temperature-compensated buried zener (DZ1) puts roughly 8.2 V on the non-inverting input of amplifier A1. A1 and a resistor network R1 to R6 scale this up to 10 V; R1, R2 and R3 are laser-trimmed to set the output exactly. The zener current comes from the regulated output through R4 (4 kΩ). No heater is used, so power stays low and warm-up is fast. Internal values: R1 22 kΩ, R2 14 kΩ, R3 8 kΩ, R4 4 kΩ, R5 50 kΩ, R6 7 kΩ.

operation.topic: Noise and the Noise Reduction pin
operation.text: Zener noise sets the output noise. A capacitor from pin 8 to ground forms a low-pass with R6 (typically 7 kΩ). With 1 µF the corner falls near 22 Hz and broadband noise measured to 1 MHz drops from about 800 µVPP to under 200 µVPP. Averaging several units cuts noise further. The 15 µs warm-up time to 0.1 % applies with pin 8 open.

Drift against temperature is specified by the box method. The box spans the specification temperatures and its diagonal slope equals the maximum specified drift; its vertical position is not known, and it lies between an upper and a lower bound. A REF102CU (2.5 ppm/°C max, −25 °C to +85 °C) has a box 2.75 mV tall, with bounds of +10.00275 V and +9.99725 V about a nominal +10.0000 V.

A low-resistance star at the common pin cuts voltage error, picked-up noise and supply-borne noise. A few ohms in the supply or ground lead have negligible effect; 0.1 Ω in an output or load-return lead is 1 mV (0.01 %) at 10 mA. V+ is bypassed with 1 µF tantalum.

The Trim pin reaches the amplifier gain through R5 (50 kΩ), whose temperature coefficient tracks R1 to R3, so trimming disturbs drift little: about 0.008 ppm/°C per mV of adjustment. A 20 kΩ potentiometer from output to common with its wiper on Trim gives at least ±300 mV; mismatch between the two halves of the potentiometer shows up in drift reduced fivefold by the internal divider, so use a mechanically stable type such as cermet. A 1 MΩ series resistor in the wiper narrows the range to about ±25 mV with finer resolution; that resistor's TCR mismatch against the internal resistors adds a little drift, small when it is much larger than 50 kΩ, and 100 ppm/°C is normally adequate.

The output sources up to 10 mA and sinks up to 5 mA, drives up to 1000 pF of load capacitance, and survives a continuous short to common or to V+. The supply runs from 11.4 V to 36 V with at most 1.4 mA of quiescent current.
Output change with time is typically 20 ppm/1000 hr in the P and U packages, falling to typically 5 ppm/1000 hr once the part has been powered for 168 hours.
The part is sensitive to electrostatic discharge; handle it with ESD precautions.
